hook_text: 3 468 fans at the match. Tomorrow the paper will say 3 500. Here is how they decided.
clip_script: Stadium in Bloemfontein, 3 468 people. The paper wants a round number. Nearest 100: 3 468 sits between 3 400 and 3 500. Look at one digit, the tens digit, 6. Six says go up. 3 500. Nearest 10? Look at the units, 8. Up. 3 470. Nearest 1 000? Look at the hundreds, 4. Four says go down. 3 000. Same crowd, three answers, and the question decides which. Now the school trip, R1 285 each, four learners. Round first: R1 300 times 4 is R5 200. Exact: R5 140. Close, so it makes sense. Write R51 400 and the estimate screams. One digit to the right: 0 to 4 down, 5 to 9 up. Round first, then calculate.
visual_style: Whiteboard number line with 3 468 sliding to the nearer mark three times; a till receipt next to a rounded estimate.
mood: Decisive, like a sports reporter on deadline.
pacing: Three fast roundings of one number, then the estimate check, then the one-line rule.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and round today's temperature, your height in centimetres and a shop price.
